passes_since_baseline.override_reason: Reviewer-directed rewrite against the new Part E classification. Piers supplied the specification; this pass applies it rather than patching sentences.

attested.notes: Rewritten against the F/D/E/J/P classification now recorded as humanise Part E. Cut, as P-class: the invented evening and letter on the desk; the manufactured fear paragraph; every tonight/tomorrow framing; the unsupported outcome claims (rarely sinks an application, plenty of directors, by the time a director calls us, we have never seen this improve); the lender mind-reading (lenders evidently accept, character test not solvency test, the rule is aimed somewhere specific); the urgency headings (The One Lender That Can Stop You, What to Check Tonight and Ask Tomorrow); and the quotable closers (the form is the thing you sign, only you can answer it in a box under a declaration you sign, the house depends on it more than the application). Scene and bite counts are deliberately low now and that is the point: what remains is F, D and labelled J. The load-bearing additions are D-class comparisons, for example that both Barclays thresholds must be met together so a 10 percent holding or a 4,000 pound judgment falls outside, and that six lenders cap personal CCJs at 500 pounds or below while the only published company threshold starts above 5,000. Domain boundary now explicit: insolvency consequences stated with practitioner authority, mortgage outcomes referred to the criteria or the broker.
